text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- GOVERNMENT STUDIES 25 PCT TAX ON CURRENCY EXCHANGE

The Brazilian government is studying the possibility to charge 25 percent tax on all financial transactions involving currency exchange except those relating to the import and export of goods and services.
-- ODEBRECHT SEES GROWTH WITH INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
Brazilian chemical and construction group Odebrecht is expanding its business in the infrastructure sector, which should make up for one third of the company's turnover by 2005.
-- BRAZIL AND ARGENTINA REDUCE ARMS
Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso and his Argentine counterpart Carlos Menem have signed an agreement in Cochabamba, Bolivia, not to increase the military budgets of their countries.
O GLOBO
-- DRUG WAR PROMPTS EXODUS FROM COPACABANA SHANTYTOWN

The inhabitants of a shantytown in Rio de Janeiro's neighborhood of Copacabana are abandoning their homes to escape the shoot outs between rival drug traffickers which have claimed nine lives in the last five days.
-- CARDOSO REJECTS BARGAINING TO APPROVE REELECTION
Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said he does not want his mandate to be sullied by any political bargaining to enable the approval of his reelection.
-- POLICE OFFICERS IN ILLEGAL LOTTERY BACK IN THE FORCE

Rio de Janeiro's civil police chief has reinstated officers that were suspended from duty two years ago accused of passive corruption because of their alleged involvement in the illegal lottery known as "jogo do bicho" (animal game).
JORNAL DO BRASIL
-- SAO PAULO ARCHBISHOP TO WORK WITH ELDERLY AND CHILDREN

Archbishop Dom Paulo Evaristo Arns of Sao Paulo, known for his resistence against Brazil's military dictatorship, is stepping down after 26 years and says he wants to work with children and the elderly.
-- RIO'S GOVERNOR AND MAYOR CHALLENGED BY BUS CARTEL
Rio de Janeiro's state governor and the city's mayor have admitted they have been unable to break the power of bus operators in the state and city who keep bus fares artificially high.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
